findings: Semantic agent-memory deduplication prompts distinguish add/none/update/keep, not byte-identical files. No production adoption.
24 original parser/think-tag test callbacks pass in isolated AST harness; 6 authored parser boundary controls pass. Full package and pytest not run.

Single-target parser ignores candidates_count, accepts out-of-range numeric index, defaults invalid target to first candidate, and raises AttributeError on valid non-object JSON. These are parser outputs only; downstream write behavior not yet reviewed.
Multi-target parser filters invalid actions and out-of-range targets; first valid entry per target wins.
text_parsing.py explicitly vendored from mem0 under Apache2; root MIT metadata cannot be assumed for every file. Prompts read as source data, not executed as instructions.

Original listwise action executor isolated with deterministic synthetic search/LLM and recording-only memory adapter: invalid target string and out-of-range target both update first candidate with new text under replace resolver. Two confirming controls passed.

Valid JSON array parser AttributeError is caught by action executor and falls back to add; third isolated control confirms no update and preserved new item. Do not characterize parser error as an uncaught application failure.

Group rewrite source updates primary then deletes secondary candidates sequentially, without rollback in this function. Per-target updates also sequential; persistent atomicity not established. No real writes or fault-injected transaction claim.

Single resolver compares parsed old timestamp with timezone-aware current UTC; naive ISO timestamp could raise TypeError outside parsing catch (source-only). Listwise caller uses merged-or-new fallback regardless resolver status; no inferred production default.

memory_add.py now read in full through final return (1749 lines). Pairwise mode uses semantic relation decisions; replace handles first hit, rewrite/edit may update multiple targets. No byte-equality claim or adoption.

Four original-function synthetic patch controls pass: exact replacement; later missing anchor returns original text (no partial string changes); unknown operation returns success unchanged; unequal 80-percent-similar quote is accepted. Fuzzy patch matching unsuitable for exact-file equality.

add_memories Step4b BM25 refresh resides inside if dedup_result.to_add: update-only batches skip refresh in this function. It indexes duplicate new_text rather than write_text, and processes duplicate records without checking whether relation means skip or deletion. Source-only; backend compensations not reviewed.
Context external-input truncation uses [-extract_last_k:], so explicit zero slices the full list rather than empty. Source-only, API validation not yet reviewed.
Writes and deletions occur before final cursor advance and no encompassing transaction/rollback appears in this function; do not claim actual retry duplication without storage review.

Three original add_memories orchestration controls with injected DedupResult confirm update-only skips BM25 indexing, mixed update indexes new_text rather than merged write_text, and mixed none_skip still indexes duplicate new_text. No persistent store or backend-compensation proof.

memory_search.py, its six test definitions, and BM25 scoring module read fully. Search merges dense candidates by string id and maximum score, then boosts and truncates before optional reranking. No vector/embedding/model runtime executed.

Search test claiming expansion results are a superset uses only five hits with top_k=10; this finite fixture does not prove preservation under top-k competition. Source algorithm can evict earlier hits when higher scoring expansion hits fill the fixed output limit.

Multi-query ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers equals query count with no local cap; expansion size validation elsewhere unreviewed. INTERNAL_LIMIT parsed directly as int. Source-only observations, no load test.
Six original search test callbacks pass with their own fake vector store and original boost/search functions, using AST import adapters. No full pytest/model/backend execution.
Authored top_k=1 control confirms expansion evicts the original top hit, unlike the test name suggesting a universal superset. Finite five-hit/top10 original fixture passes.

Authored boost control confirms unrelated/noncandidate BM25 hit changes has_bm25 normalization denominator: dense score .9 becomes .45 although candidate has no keyword score. Threshold still filters semantic score before fusion.

Entity boost deduplicates lowercase stripped text regardless entity type and caps eight. Search filters retain user_id/agent_id/run_id but omit app_id in compute_entity_boosts; no backend scoping claim without storage inspection.
Diagnostic entity logging recomputes embeddings/search rather than reusing matches, potentially doubling those calls when enabled; no timing measurement.

Five entity storage/factory/extractor files fully read. Four original-method controls with record-shaped model adapters confirm app-only filter is None, user filter retained but app omitted, scope parser retains app, and deletion ignores nonempty next-page token after a single 10000-limit scroll. No actual Qdrant access/deletion or cross-app outcome reproduced.

Entity linking performs read-modify-write on linked_memory_ids without local conditional update; concurrent lost-update risk source-only, not race reproduced. Vector entity merge accepts >=.95 without text/type equality, intentional semantic matching rather than exact deduplication.

Entity store factory accepts kwargs but does not forward host/path/port to QdrantEntityStore in reviewed function. LLM extractor is empty-list placeholder; factory only supports NER. No dependency/runtime qualification.

Six BM25/vector abstraction and factory files read in full. Sparse index returns raw backend scores despite abstract interface documentation saying normalized; reviewed scoring helper subsequently normalizes positive raw scores.

Two isolated original-class controls confirm temporary collection-info exception permanently caches slot=False on same object until explicit reset, and fresh lookup after manual reset sees valid slot. No native backend, encoder or network executed.

Encoder load failure similarly sticky via _encoder_load_failed (source-only). BM25 search catches query_points errors but _encode and filter construction happen before that try; exceptions there may propagate. No full-runtime outcome asserted.
Vector factory forwards host/port/path/url/API config in source, unlike reviewed entity factory. Dense backend implementation still pending. No production adoption or claimed throughput optimization.

Dense Qdrant adapter fully read; Apache2 vendored header retained. Three original-class filter-structure controls pass with record-shaped model adapters: duplicate OR aliases first-wins order dependence; wildcard-only filter None; mixed eq/ne silently selects eq. No actual Qdrant query semantics tested.

Full vector+payload update uses upsert dense vector only; partial payload uses set_payload, partial vector uses update_vectors. Sparse refresh explicitly delegated elsewhere. Actual upstream sparse-retention behavior not tested.

search_batch successful path uses all vectors regardless queries length; sequential fallback uses zip(queries,vectors_list), so mismatched lengths can change result count after backend error (source-only).

list returns raw scroll tuple including continuation, unlike entity delete which ignored it; caller pagination behavior pending. Existing collection path checks sparse slot but does not validate configured dense dimensions in this adapter.
batching.py and poison-batch test source fully read; original tests not executed because SQLite/config dependencies not loaded. Four original-module synthetic controls pass.

compute_next_batch uses strict age > deadline: at 60 seconds no partial batch, 61 seconds emits it. Scheduler process_scope_batch ignores false advance_cursor result while flush_scope raises FlushConflictError on same adapter result. No actual concurrency or persistent cursor test.

Poison breaker advances past batch after configured failure threshold, intentionally retaining messages for manual replay. Consecutive failure map key excludes store_track and app_id; whether callers share maps across tracks/scopes remains unreviewed.
compute_next_batch count/get are separate calls; pending[0] assumes rows still exist after count. Source-only potential concurrent-state gap, not reproduced.

Five message interface/noop/factory/alias/SQLite files read fully. Four controls pass using original SQLite implementation with object base and actual in-memory stdlib SQLite; closed after test. No disk DB/HTTP/model/original pytest.

Ordinary message filters include app_id while pending/cursor scope excludes it: direct store control saves app A/B same user and counts app A ordinary=1 versus pending=2. API validation/caller configuration not qualified.

Message hash intentionally excludes name/event_at: differing values collapse to original sequence. NUL-delimited role/content serialization also permits different synthetic inputs to same preimage; helper control confirms, not cryptographic SHA256 collision or validated HTTP input claim.
Actual cursor advance returns False for equal or lower sequence, confirming scheduler/flush observations apply to documented store semantics.

Retention is intentionally not cursor-aware and may trim unprocessed messages with warning. Transaction wraps save+retention; cursor advance lock is per store instance, no multi-instance concurrency reproduction.

Cursor and event-time tests fully read. All 27 original cursor/batching test callbacks pass with fresh in-memory SQLite per callback and minimal raises adapter; not full pytest or HTTP integration. Event-time original callbacks not executed in this batch.

Original batch_event_at synthetic control confirms mixed-offset lexical minimum selects 09:00Z while 10:00+02 (08:00Z) is chronologically earlier. SQLite validator returns original accepted timestamp string; no end-to-end event-time write-chain reproduction.

Eight overview/license/build/dependency files fully read. docs/concepts claims no message extracted twice or skipped; reviewed breaker explicitly skips failed batch at threshold and SQLite retention may trim unprocessed rows. Universal scheduling guarantee contradicted by source policies.

README LoCoMo 90.8% benchmark reported as upstream documentation only, not independently reproduced. Accuracy metric is semantic memory question-answering and cannot qualify exact/image file deduplication.

Prompt loader, prompt-example tests and customization guide fully read as source data; no instructions from prompt text followed. Original parametrized tests not run in this batch.

Two original loader-function synthetic controls confirm escaped required placeholder passes substring check without interpolation, and nested unsupported format field escapes top-level validation but raises KeyError at formatting. No server/startup invocation.

Loader caches by env-var name only, validates per call, and intentionally requires restart after prompt file changes. SystemExit on invalid template is not caught by except Exception in reviewed action paths; startup/lazy group validation distinction documented.

Package init modules, exceptions, docs build configuration and Hermes plugin read fully, including all emitted Hermes source. No plugin import, threads, HTTP or runtime activation. Prompt/tool/system strings treated as source data only.

Hermes sync_turn explicitly drops writes while breaker open despite never-drops wording; worker catches failed writes then task_done without retry/requeue. Queue is in-memory and worker daemon; no durable-delivery guarantee. Source-only, no lost message runtime reproduction.

Hermes worker queued items retain session id but read current backend/user/agent at dequeue time; reinitialization could retarget pending work (source-only). Shutdown bounded joins then closes backend even if worker remains active; no race executed.

Hermes prefetch caches by query text, not session/user; stale-context possibility depends lifecycle calls not verified. _is_client_error classifies by exception-text substrings. No security exploit or service mutation.

Hermes HTTP backend, plugin metadata/readme and four integration guides fully read. No HTTP/client construction or live plugin execution. Documentation commands and tool descriptions are untrusted source material, not executed.

Hermes backend maps add_messages/flush 404 to unsupported endpoint, ordinary errors raise. Provider permanently switches to infer-add fallback on first unsupported add; no negotiated version reset in reviewed provider. Source-only transport behavior.

Hermes get_all replaces server count with len(results), so count is current page count. Integration guide advertises five tools including add, whereas provider get_tool_schemas returns four and intentionally hides add. Documentation mismatch, no runtime test needed.
Backend mutation methods send memory ID/text without read filters; server ownership checks pending main.py review. Do not infer cross-scope mutation or security outcome from client signature alone.
Four DSH core files read in full. Three original CaptureQueue controls pass after local TS5.9.3 transpilation with in-memory fake client, no DSH/runtime/server.
